claims.proposition_evaluated: At its August 26, 2026 meeting, Edmonton's Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing every approved public speaker's maximum time from the five minutes in the Council Procedures Bylaw to three minutes for that meeting, with 60 to 80 approved-speaker entries on bike-lane item 7.6.
claims.interpretation_notes: The committee, rather than City Council, made the motion. I counted entries, not distinct people. Item 2.3 lists item 7.6 in five panels of 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64 approved entries, within both the primary 60–80 band and alternative 50–90 band. For all meeting items, N-all = 5 (7.1) + 1 (7.3) + 9 (7.4, including one additional-speaker motion) + 64 (7.6) = 79 entries: Supported under either band. For item 7.6 presentations, N-spoke = 16 + 16 + 17 + 2 = 51 entries: Partially supported under 60–80 because the queue magnitude fails, and Supported under 50–90. The result is definition-sensitive if 'queue' means people who spoke. N-all can count a person twice if approved on two items.

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) sets a five-minute maximum for each approved speaker. Section 4 permits a Standing Committee to modify the bylaw by special resolution; section 2 defines that as at least two-thirds of all committee members voting in favour.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Bylaw 18155, Council Procedures Bylaw, consolidated October 29, 2025
supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing limit and mechanism for changing it.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4, M. Janz moved to adjust section 38 for the August 26 meeting: each approved speaker could speak for at most three minutes; each Council member had three minutes for questions and three to speak to or close debate on a motion. E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack and A. Paquette voted in favour; none opposed. It carried 6–0. The header lists six committee members, so 6 ÷ 6 exceeds the two-thirds requirement.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Committee post-meeting minutes, items 1.4 and 1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: A valid, meeting-wide three-minute maximum for every approved speaker. The motion precedes item 2.3's Requests to Speak motion and the first item 7.6 presentation in the minutes.
supporting_evidence.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

supporting_evidence.finding: Item 2.3 approves 64 entries for item 7.6: panels 1–4 have 15 each and panel 5 has four. Fifteen entries carry organizations: panel 1, Edmonton Bike Coalition and YEG Bike Coalition; panel 2, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, YEG Bike Coalition, Paths for People and Ward Métis Bikes (three entries); panel 3, Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton and YEG Bike Coalition; panel 4, Paths for People and YEG Bike Coalition.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The primary approved-speaker count and its organization entries.

challenging_evidence.finding: Item 7.6 records 51 presentation entries, rather than approximately 70, across four panels of 16, 16, 17 and 2. This challenges the reported magnitude only if 'queue' means people recorded as having spoken; it does not change the primary approved-speaker count.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The alternative N-spoke is below the primary 60–80 band.

limitations: Reviewed the carried minutes for items 1.4, 2.3, 2.4 and 7.6 as supplied on October 2, 2026. A direct portal request returned HTTP 403. No correction to those items appears in the carried text; the remainder of the meeting page was not supplied.

A direct request for the bylaw PDF returned HTTP 502. Search-indexed text of the City's PDF exposed the operative sections, but I could not inspect its full amendment list. I found no post-October 29, 2025 amendment to section 38 in targeted searches; that is not an exhaustive legislative check.

The supplied minutes record no individual speaking durations or extension motion in items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6. Five public-speaker attachments are listed under item 7.6. The excluded items and unplayed meeting video limit any meeting-wide absence claim.

For context, I searched City-indexed post-meeting minutes for section 38 adjustments since October 29, 2025. City Council's January 27 and February 17, 2026 minutes record adjustments to councillors' speaking limits, including three-minute question periods; those examples did not reduce public-speaker time. This was a targeted search, not a review of every meeting.
The minutes and agenda record no reason for the August 26 motion. I did not verify the meeting video's spoken discussion.
unknowns: Why the motion was moved and whether the queue's size caused it.
How long each person actually spoke, and whether a limit was enforced differently for anyone.
Speakers' positions, place of residence, physical presence or organizational role.
Distinct-person counts across items or between the approval and presentation lists.

missing_evidence.description: An authenticated, accessible full bylaw consolidation and any later amending bylaws through August 26, 2026, to confirm section 38's amendment history.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

missing_evidence.description: An accessible official recording or verified transcript to establish any oral explanation and individual speaking times.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

calculations_needed: Special-resolution vote: 6 in favour ÷ 6 listed committee members = 100%, above two-thirds.
what_would_change_my_verdict: An authenticated correction changing the item 7.6 approved-entry count outside 60–80 would make the primary proposition partially supported.
An amendment effective by August 26 that changed section 38's five-minute standing limit, or an authenticated correction reversing or narrowing the motion, would require a new verdict.
claims.suggested_one_line: Yes. The Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 to cut each approved speaker's maximum from five to three minutes for its August 26 meeting; 64 entries were approved for the bike-lane item.
claims.suggested_short_answer: The bylaw allowed each approved speaker up to five minutes. Before approving speakers, the Infrastructure Committee carried M. Janz's motion setting a three-minute maximum for all approved speakers at that meeting. Its item 7.6 list held 64 approved entries, within the stated 'about seventy' range; the minutes record 51 presentation entries. The vote and counts do not establish why the committee acted, which side speakers supported, or how long any person actually spoke.
